newsitem.title: FRANCE: Private Europe military plane funds seen possible.
newsitem.headline: Private Europe military plane funds seen possible.

text.p: A senior executive of British Aerospace Plc said on Thursday a proposal to raise private sector funds to pay for the development of the planned military European Future Large Aircraft was realistic.
BAe wants to build the plane along with France's state-owned SNI Aerospatiale.

"If governments were prepared to give us a contract for development and production together, we can enter into a fixed priced contract with a guaranteed performance specification," John Weston, BAe group managing director told a business conference.

"(If) we've got government contracts that we can take to the financial market and we can get funding...the governments will pay for the development in the unit price of the airplane in exactly the same way as they do if they buy a staff car from Peugeot or Renault or anybody else," he said.
"The concept being talked about in France is a very realistic concept; it's a concept we may need to use in other countries," he said.
France and Germany for budgetary reasons have axed development funds for the plane, which is designed to meet tactical transport needs of eight European armies.
Weston said BAe's studies for the British army showed that the plane, even with development costs on top of the purchase price, would be cheaper than buying off-the-shelf from the United States.

The plane "is capable of doing that work twice as cost effectively as either of the two American airplanes," he said, referring to the C130J Hercules from Lockheed Martin Corp and the C17 from McDonnell Douglas Corp.
